options.whyWrong: $5\pi/6$ is outside $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$, so $\sin^{-1}$ can't return it.
$\sin(5\pi/6)$ is positive, so the answer must be positive.

questions.solution:
**Key idea:** the principal range of $\sin^{-1}$ is $\left[-\tfrac{\pi}{2}, \tfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

1. $\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6} = \sin\left(\pi - \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\right) = \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac12$
2. $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ lies in the principal range → **$\dfrac{\pi}{6}$**
hints: Which angle in $[-\pi/2, \pi/2]$ has the same sine as $5\pi/6$?
